description: PLAN ONLY (no implementation yet): an agent-led robot research loop. The north-star outcome: a model we can put any task in front of, and it just works on the task until it's done. How we get there is open. Setup to plan: a strong LLM agent leads the research (with Jake's input) and has (a) exact joint-level control of the SO-101 arms and our hand, (b) rented GPUs, (c) lots of data, (d) an open generalist starting model (MolmoAct2 first, per the plans). The agent can request whatever it needs: Jake or other humans recording demonstrations (filed as human-lane pebbles, e.g. 'record 20 demos of the cup pick'), its own scripted motions, autonomous practice, sim, training runs. The core requirement is that improvement is VERIFIABLE. Plan the scoreboard first: a held-out task suite never trained on, fixed reset start states, automatic camera-judged pass/fail, enough trials per round to separate real gains from noise, and success-rate trend tracking. Cover: auto-reset fixtures, data-request workflow, compute budget, safety/hardware wear, the human-mirror setup (two eye-height stereo cameras), and a first narrow milestone that proves the loop climbs. Output: plans/agent_led_research.md, for Jake to review before anything is built.

user_request.name: The AI is leading the research, with some of my input, and it can get whatever it needs: me or other humans running tons of demonstrations, or controlling the arm itself. The key is that it's verifiable that it's improving. It's just a plan for now. The fundamental thing is I don't care how it happens, but we need to end up with a model where we can set a task in front of it and it will just work on the task and get it done.
